text_blocks.snippet: Losartan is a prescription medication used to treat high blood pressure, protect the kidneys in type 2 diabetes, and lower the risk of stroke. While generally well-tolerated, it can cause several side effects.
Most common side effects are mild and tend to improve as your body adjusts to the medication:

list.snippet: Dizziness or lightheadedness (especially when standing up quickly)
Upper respiratory symptoms (such as a stuffy or runny nose, sore throat, or cold-like symptoms)
Digestive issues (such as nausea, diarrhea, or mild stomach upset)

text_blocks.snippet: Seek immediate medical attention or contact your healthcare provider right away if you experience:

list.snippet: Allergic reactions (anaphylaxis): Swelling of the face, lips, tongue, throat, or eyes, or severe difficulty breathing or swallowing.
High potassium levels (hyperkalemia): Muscle weakness, confusion, or a fast or irregular heartbeat.
Kidney problems: A sudden decrease in urination or swelling in your hands, ankles, or feet.
Very low blood pressure (hypotension): Fainting, severe lightheadedness, or extreme wooziness.
Liver problems: Yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice) or severe upper stomach pain.
Pregnancy Warning: Losartan should not be taken during pregnancy as it can cause serious injury or death to an unborn baby.

Interactions: Avoid starting potassium supplements, potassium salt substitutes, or NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) without talking to your doctor, as they can interact with losartan or worsen kidney and potassium levels.
Consult a Doctor: Review official details on the Mayo Clinic Losartan Guide or speak with your pharmacist or doctor before making any changes to your medication.
